title: Trump and Xi: Strongmen at the Temple of Thymos
author: Michael Kovrig
text:
U.S. President Donald Trump tours the Temple of Heaven in Beijing with China’s President Xi Jinping, May 14, 2026.
Credit: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok
When U.S. President Donald Trump made his second state visit to China in May 2026, Xi Jinping escorted him through Beijing’s magisterial Temple of Heaven, where the Ming and Qing emperors performed rites that mediated between heaven and the earthly order. But when these two men with autocratic impulses and outsized egos strolled through the complex, it became not a Temple of Heaven but a Temple of Thymos – a stage for distributing recognition rather than cosmic concerns. Now, the neoclassical architecture of the White House provides the set for their September 23–25 encounter. Readers of The Diplomat can find in it many articles on the “Thucydides Trap” popularized by the political scientist Graham Allison. The Thucydides Trap suggests that China and the United States are headed for inevitable conflict. Several scholars dispute Allison’s reading, and yet the ancient historian’s ghost still hovered as Xi and Trump moved through the temple, with the Chinese Communist Party’s general secretary, who has a pattern of citing Allison, even referencing the phrase.I want to propose a lens for power rivalry that’s equally ancient but different and complementary: a Thymos Trap. [...]
